svg.aria-label: Every part on the pod board, colour-coded by function, on both faces, with a legend explaining what each part is and why it is needed.
svg.text: Every part on the pod board, and why it is there
20 × 11.5 mm, drawn 30× from the draft board file. Colour = job. Gold = copper pads. Front of the pod (toward your eye) is on the left of the outer face and the right of the inner face.
Inner face (toward the cell), seen from below
black dot, both faces = the mic sound port: a hole straight through the board
the MCU and the parts that keep it stable
runs everything: filters the mic, does the FFT, makes the tones, times
decoupling: a charge reservoir right at a supply pin, so current spikes
decoupling for another VDD pin (one per pin: each pin's spikes are local)
decoupling for the third VDD pin
bulk store for the whole chip: covers slower dips the 100 nF ones can't
VDDA (the analog supply): smooths it for the battery-voltage ADC
on NRST (reset): stops noise from resetting the chip
holds BOOT0 low so the chip starts our program, not ST's bootloader
the accurate reference the 80 MHz clock is locked to: both ears then
crystal load capacitor: sets the exact oscillation frequency
the MCU's own 1.1 V switching supply
the energy store of the chip's built-in buck converter (3.0 → 1.1 V)
buck input capacitor: supplies its 3 MHz current pulses locally
buck output capacitor: smooths the 1.1 V core supply
hears 20–85 kHz; outputs a 1-bit stream at 4 MHz; ports through a hole
the mic's decoupling: a clean supply means a quiet mic
in series with the 4 MHz mic clock: softens its edges so it radiates

one half of the H-bridge: switches transducer end A between 3.0 V and
the other half: end B. A and B in antiphase = ±3 V across the coil
gate pull-up: keeps Q1's P-FET off while the MCU boots (its pins float
gate pull-down: keeps Q1's N-FET off at reset (no shoot-through at
protects the bridge from static on the transducer wire (it touches your
local reservoir for the bridge's current peaks, so they don't pull the
charges the LiPo safely: constant current, then constant 4.2 V, then
sets the charge current: 1000 V / 22 kΩ = 45 mA (gentle for a 105 mAh
clamps static and reverse polarity on the exposed charge contacts
charge contact + (5 V from the dock)

turns 3.3–4.2 V from the cell into a steady 3.0 V, very quietly (7 µV
LDO output capacitor: it needs one to stay stable
your input, and how full the cell is
top of a divider: halves the battery voltage so the ADC can read it
bottom of the divider (2 µA total drain)
holds the divider's voltage steady while the ADC samples it
holds the button line low until pressed, so it never reads a phantom
